guide.q.standard_vs_daily_listings: What's the difference between standard and daily listings?
guide.a.standard_vs_daily_listings:
A standard listing is a one-off. Attendees book a place, and the people limit covers the whole listing.

A daily listing lets attendees pick a date when they book. The people limit applies to each date on its own, so you can run the same listing every day with a fresh set of places.
guide.a.what_are_groups:
Groups show related listings together on one page, at one address. Create a group on the Groups page, then tick the groups a listing belongs to using the Group checkboxes on the listing form — a listing can be in more than one group at once.

Share /ticket/your-group-slug and attendees see every open listing in the group on one page. All listings in a group must be the same type (all daily or all standard).

Set an optional Max Attendees on the group to cap total bookings across every listing in it. Terms and conditions added to a group replace the global ones for that page.
guide.q.listing_date_and_location: What are the listing date and location fields for?
guide.a.listing_date_and_location:
These are optional fields you can fill in when you create or edit a listing. The date is when it happens, and the location is where. Both appear on the attendee's ticket page, so they know when and where to go.

For daily listings, attendees already pick a date when booking, so the date field is more useful for standard one-off listings.
guide.q.max_tickets_per_purchase: What does 'max tickets per purchase' do?
guide.a.max_tickets_per_purchase: It sets how many tickets one person can book in one go. For example, setting it to 4 lets someone book up to 4 places at once. The quantity picker on the booking form never goes above this number or above the places left.
guide.a.what_are_modifiers:
Modifiers change the price at checkout without editing the listing's own price. Open Modifiers to make discounts, extra charges, promo codes, returning-customer offers, or optional extras.

A modifier can apply to the whole order, to chosen listings, or to every listing in chosen groups.

Each modifier has a trigger — what makes it apply. Automatic applies whenever its rules match. Promo code applies when the buyer types the matching code. Optional add-on is one the buyer can choose on the booking form. Question answer applies when the buyer picks a linked answer to a custom question — for example a delivery area. You can also limit a modifier with a minimum order amount, a minimum number of past bookings, how many are left, and whether it is switched on.
guide.a.how_modifier_values_work:
The Type decides how the Value is read:

  • Fixed amount: enter an amount in your currency. For example, 10 means a 10.00 charge or discount, depending on the Direction.
  • Percentage: enter the number only. For example, 10 means 10% of the subtotal the modifier covers. Percentages must be greater than 0. A discount can be at most 100. A charge can be at most 10,000.
  • Multiplier: enter how many times to multiply the price. For example, 1.5 makes the price 1.5 times bigger, 0.5 makes it half price, and 10 makes it 10 times bigger. Direction is ignored for multipliers, because the factor itself says whether the price rises or falls.

Modifiers work from the original subtotal they cover, and do not stack on each other. The booking fee is then calculated on the final modified subtotal.
guide.a.registration_deadlines:
Set a "closes at" date and time on your listing. After that moment, the booking form shows a "registration closed" message and takes no more bookings.

If someone opens the form before the deadline but sends it after, their booking is refused too.
guide.q.embed_booking_form: How do I put the booking form on my own website?
guide.a.embed_booking_form:
Embedding means showing your booking form inside your own website's page. Your listing page shows two embed codes. You need only one of them, not both:

  • Embed Script (recommended) — paste a single <script> tag into your page, and it builds the form for you, resizing itself as needed.
  • Embed Iframe — use this if your website blocks outside scripts, or you want full control over the frame's look.

In Settings, add your website's address to the embed hosts list to limit which websites can show your forms. With no hosts listed, any website can embed them.
guide.q.manually_add_attendee: How do I manually add an attendee?
guide.a.manually_add_attendee: Open the listing page and scroll down to Add Attendee. Fill in the name and contact details, set the quantity, and submit. The attendee is added straight away, without the booking form or any payment. Handy for walk-ins, free guests, or corrections.
guide.q.custom_redirect_after_booking: How do I send people to my own page after booking?
guide.a.custom_redirect_after_booking:
When you create or edit a listing, enter an address in the "thank you URL" field. After a booking or payment finishes, attendees go to that address instead of the usual confirmation page.

The address must start with https://, or be a path starting with /.
guide.q.add_listing_image: How do I add an image to a listing?
guide.a.add_listing_image: When you create or edit a listing, use the image upload field to attach a picture. It appears on the booking page and in the public listings list. You can use JPEG, PNG, and WebP pictures.
guide.q.add_file_attachment: How do I add a file to a listing?
guide.q.listing_qr_code: Where can I find the listing QR code?
guide.a.listing_qr_code: On the listing's page, click the QR code link next to the public address. It opens a picture of the QR code that links to your booking page. Save it or print it for posters and flyers.
guide.q.duplicate_listing: How do I copy a listing?
guide.a.duplicate_listing: Open the listing and click Duplicate. This makes a new listing with the same people limit, price, fields, group, and other settings, so you change only what you need. The name is left blank for you to fill in. The image, attachment, and assigned questions are not copied.
guide.q.deactivate_listing: How do I switch a listing off?
guide.a.deactivate_listing: Open the listing and click Deactivate. Switched-off listings take no bookings and are hidden from the public listings list, but all attendee data is kept. Click Reactivate to make it bookable again.
guide.a.non_transferable_tickets: When you switch on Non-Transferable on a listing, attendees see a notice on their ticket: "Non-transferable — ID required at entry". At the door, the scanner asks staff to check that the attendee's ID matches the name on the ticket before checking them in. This helps stop ticket touts.
guide.q.edit_attendee: How do I edit an attendee?
guide.a.edit_attendee:
Open the listing's attendee list, find the attendee, and click Edit. The edit page has three sections:

  • Contact Information — name, email, phone, address, special instructions, and custom question answers. These are shared across all the attendee's listings.
  • Listing Registrations — a table of each listing the attendee is booked on, with their quantity, check-in status, and refund status. You can change the quantity per listing or remove a registration.
  • Add to Listing — link the attendee to another listing. For daily listings you also pick a date. Places are checked when adding.
guide.q.add_terms_and_conditions: How do I add terms and conditions?
guide.a.add_terms_and_conditions: In Settings, enter your terms in the "Terms and Conditions" box. When set, attendees must tick an agreement box before they can book. Clear the box to remove the requirement.
guide.a.what_are_custom_booking_question: Custom booking questions let you ask attendees a question with set answers during booking — for example "Which meal would you like?" with answers "Meat", "Veggie", and "Vegan". The attendee must pick one before they can finish booking.
guide.q.create_question: How do I create a question?
guide.a.create_question: Open any listing and click Questions in the listing menu, then follow the Manage Questions link. Type your question and click Add question. Then open the question and add your answers. You can reorder the answers with the move-up and move-down buttons.
guide.q.add_question_to_listing: How do I add a question to a listing?
guide.a.add_question_to_listing: Open the listing and click Questions. Tick the questions you want on that listing's booking form and save. One question can be shared by many listings — create it once and assign it wherever you need it.
guide.q.share_questions_between_listings: Can I share questions between listings?
guide.a.share_questions_between_listings: Yes. Questions are created on their own and then assigned to listings, so one question can appear on as many listings as you like. Change the question or its answers, and it updates everywhere it is used.
guide.q.where_to_see_answers: Where do I see the answers?
guide.a.where_to_see_answers: Answers appear in the attendee table on listing and group pages, so you can see at a glance what each attendee chose. They are also shown on the attendee's own page and included in the CSV export.
guide.q.combine_multiple_listings: How do I combine multiple listings into one booking?
guide.a.combine_multiple_listings:
For most collections of listings, use a group instead. See What are groups? in the Listings section. A group gives you one address that stays the same. Attendees can book several of its listings in one form.

A multi-booking link suits a one-off combination. To make one, open Listings in the admin menu and scroll to the Multi-booking link section at the bottom of the page. Tick the listings you want. The link updates as you tick. The listings appear in the link in the order you tick them.

The link joins the listings' slugs with a + in the address — a slug is the last part of a listing's address. For example /ticket/listing-one+listing-two.

Attendees see a single form. They fill in their details once and book all the listings together. If any are paid, they pay once for the total.

The attendee gets a single ticket with one QR code covering all their listings, and their ticket page shows one card per listing. In the admin, they appear as one attendee linked to several listings.

If the listings collect different contact details, the combined form asks for everything any of them collects — pair an email-only listing with one that also collects a phone number, and every attendee must give both. The fields always appear in the same order (email, phone, address, special instructions).
guide.q.facebook_403_error: Why do I get a 403 error when sharing my link on Facebook?
guide.a.facebook_403_error:
When you first share a link from a new domain on Facebook, Facebook may refuse it with a 403 error. That is Facebook's own rule about unfamiliar domains — the error comes from Facebook and never reaches your site.

To fix it, paste your link into the Facebook Sharing Debugger and click Scrape Again if the result looks wrong. After Facebook has read the page once, later shares work normally.
guide.a.what_is_public_site:
When switched on in Settings, your site gets its own public website, with pages for Home and Listings, plus Terms and Contact pages if you have set them up. The Listings page shows every open listing with booking links. Visitors can read the details and book straight away.

With the public site off, visitors can still book through direct ticket links.
guide.q.hide_listing_from_public_list: Can I hide a listing from the public list?
guide.a.hide_listing_from_public_list:
Yes. When editing a listing, tick Hidden Listing. Hidden listings do not appear on the public Listings page, and search engines are told to leave their ticket pages alone. While the listing is active, it can still be booked through its own link or when embedded in another website.

By default, a group's booking page still sells a hidden listing inside it. Edit the group and empty the Show hidden listings on this group's booking page box to keep it off the group page too. The listing's own link keeps working while it is active.
guide.q.edit_homepage_and_contact: How do I edit the homepage and contact page?
guide.a.edit_homepage_and_contact:
Switch on the public site in Settings, then open the Site section in the admin navigation.

The homepage editor sets the website title (the heading on all public pages) and the homepage text. The contact page editor sets your contact details. Both fields understand Markdown formatting.
guide.a.what_is_purchase_only_mode:
When you switch on No check-in on a listing, buyers get the item without an entry ticket. This suits raffles, fundraisers, donations, merchandise, digital products — anything that does not need someone scanned at a door. The booking button changes from "Reserve" to "Buy now", and after purchase buyers see "Your Purchase" instead of "Your Tickets".

Because nobody needs checking in, QR codes, the scanner, and wallet passes (Apple & Google) are all hidden. The listing is also left out of the calendar and news feeds. Non-transferable ID notices are hidden too — there is no door to check at.
guide.q.how_do_i_merge_duplicate_attende: How do I merge duplicate attendees?
guide.a.how_do_i_merge_duplicate_attende:
If the same person booked twice and ended up with two records, you can merge them into one. Open one attendee's edit page and find the Merge section. Enter the other attendee's ticket token — the code from their ticket link — to start.

You then see both records side by side: contact details, question answers, and listings. For each difference, choose which value to keep. Matching data is kept automatically. When you confirm, the second attendee is deleted and everything chosen lands in the first.
guide.q.how_do_i_add_an_attendee_to: How do I add an attendee to another listing?
guide.a.how_do_i_add_an_attendee_to: Open the attendee's edit page and use the Add to Listing section at the bottom. Select the listing, choose a quantity, and for daily listings pick a date. If the listing has room, the attendee is linked straight away.
guide.q.how_do_i_remove_an_attendee_from: How do I remove an attendee from a listing?
guide.a.how_do_i_remove_an_attendee_from: On the attendee's edit page, find the listing in the Listing Registrations table and click Remove. If the attendee is booked on other listings, they stay in the system. If it was their only listing, the attendee is deleted entirely.
guide.q.how_do_i_delete_an_attendee: How do I delete an attendee?
guide.a.how_do_i_delete_an_attendee:
Open the listing's attendee list and click Delete next to the attendee. You will see a page showing their name, email, quantity, and registration date. Type the attendee's exact name to confirm, then click Delete Attendee. This removes the attendee and their payment record for good. Their rows in Money stay — checkout and refund records cannot be changed or deleted.

If the attendee has paid, refund them first — once deleted, there is no payment record to refund against. See the Refunds section below.
guide.q.how_do_i_resend_a_confirmation_e: How do I resend a confirmation email?
guide.a.how_do_i_resend_a_confirmation_e:
In the listing's attendee list, click Re-send Notification next to the attendee. You type their name to confirm. This sends both the attendee's confirmation email (with their ticket link) and your notification email.

If email is not set up, or the attendee gave no email address, nothing is sent.
guide.q.listing_in_multiple_groups: Can a listing be in more than one group?
guide.a.listing_in_multiple_groups: Yes. A listing's groups are a set of checkboxes on its edit form, not a single choice — tick every group it should belong to. The same listing can appear on several group pages, and when a group is sold as a package, the listing can carry a different package price in each one.
guide.a.what_are_listing_defaults:
Open Listing Defaults (owner only) to set the values new listings start with — bookable days, minimum notice, how far ahead dates show, webhook and thank-you addresses, and whether new listings are hidden.

Each listing has a single Use defaults switch. While it is on, those fields are hidden on that listing and follow the defaults. Defaults apply live, not copied: change one here and every listing with the switch on updates itself. Leave a field as No default to keep deciding it per listing.
guide.q.listing_page_tabs: Where do I find a listing's attendees, QR code and actions?
guide.a.listing_page_tabs: Each listing (and each attendee) opens as one page with a row of tabs across the top. A listing's tabs are Overview, Attendees, Edit, Questions, Booking QR, Activity and Actions (copy, export, scanner, refund all, switch off, delete). You only see the tabs your role can open, so an editor lands straight on Edit.
guide.a.what_are_add_ons:
A listing can require the buyer to choose from a set of other listings when booking — one child for each unit they book. For example, a booking on a meal listing could require choosing one drink.

Set them on the listing's Edit tab under Advanced settings → Required child listings: tick the listings to offer, then Save required children. Children take the parent's date and duration, and one child can be offered under several parents.

Nesting is one level deep — a child cannot itself have children, and a daily child needs a daily parent.
guide.q.bookable_alone: What does “Can Be Booked By Itself” mean?
guide.a.bookable_alone:
By default, once a listing is used as another listing's child, it loses its own booking page — buyers can only reach it inside the parent's booking.

Tick Can Be Booked By Itself on the child's edit form to keep its own booking page and public listing card as well as offering it as an add-on. Leave it off for an extra or upgrade that should only ever be sold alongside its parent.
guide.q.modifier_value_precision: What amounts can I enter for a modifier's value?
guide.a.modifier_value_precision: Enter a fixed Value and the optional Minimum order in your own currency (for example 10.00), using the number of decimal places that currency uses. An amount with too many decimals is refused with an error, not quietly rounded. Percentage and multiplier modifiers are not currency amounts, so they keep their full precision.
guide.q.question_descriptions: Can a booking question have a longer description?
guide.a.question_descriptions: Yes. The Question Text field understands formatting, so a question can include bold text, links, lists, or several paragraphs. A short single line shows as the field's label. A longer, formatted description shows as a block of text above the input, properly labelled for screen readers.
guide.a.what_are_site_pages: Pages are your own pages on the public site — a title, some text, and optional search-engine fields — that live at their own address and can list chosen listings, groups, and other pages. Manage them under Site → Pages.
guide.q.build_site_page: How do I build a Page and add it to the menu?
guide.a.build_site_page:
Go to Site → Pages and choose Add Page. On the page's edit screen, use Add to this page to attach listings, groups, or other pages, and reorder or remove them under Contents.

Top-level pages appear in your site's menu (you can reorder them on the list). A page becomes a sub-page by being added to another page, and the menu shows that nesting. Deleting a page moves its sub-pages up to the top level.
guide.q.news_posts: How do I post news on my public site?
guide.a.news_posts:
Open Site → News to write news posts. Each post has a name, an optional short snippet, optional search-engine fields, and a body, and you can attach pictures from your image library — the first becomes the post's picture, and extra ones show as a small gallery under it.

Once at least one post exists, the public site shows a News link to /news, which lists every post with its name, snippet, and picture, newest first. Readers can also follow the news feed at /feeds/news.rss.
guide.q.group_vs_package: What's the difference between a group and a package?
guide.a.group_vs_package: A plain group shows several listings on one shared page. A package is a group with Sell this group as a package switched on: it is booked as one bundle. Each member listing gets its own price per unit and a set quantity in each package, and the buyer chooses how many packages to book. Pay-what-you-want listings cannot be packaged.
guide.q.sell_group_as_package: How do I sell a group as a package?
guide.a.sell_group_as_package: Create the group and add its listings, then open the group's Edit form and tick Sell this group as a package. A Package prices table appears with one row per member. Set each member's Per-unit price and Qty per package, then save. Members with customisable days also show a per-day price for each booking length.
guide.q.package_member_pricing: How do per-member package prices and quantities work?
guide.a.package_member_pricing:
For each member: leave Per-unit price blank to charge the listing's own price (shown as the placeholder), enter 0 to make it free inside this package, or enter an amount to set its price for this package only.

Qty per package is how many of that listing one package includes (at least 1). The settings are stored per group, so the same listing can be priced differently in different packages.
guide.q.hide_package_listings: How do I hide listing names within a package?
guide.a.hide_package_listings:
Tick Hide listing names within package on the group's edit form. The package's booking page, tickets, and confirmation emails then show only the package name.

A listing can still appear on the public listings page and use its own booking page — its Hidden Listing setting controls that separately.

A package that has sold hidden-name tickets must keep its package record. Show the listing names before you un-package or delete it.
guide.q.package_capacity: How do I cap total bookings on a package?
guide.a.package_capacity: Set Max Attendees on the group. It limits the combined attendee count across every listing in the group, not each listing separately. The group's detail page shows a Group Attendees row with the current count, the cap, and how many remain.
guide.q.sell_time_slots: How do I sell several time slots on the same day?
guide.a.sell_time_slots:
Make one listing for each time, and put the time in its name — for example Session at 10am and Session at 2pm. Set each one to Daily, then tick the days it runs under Bookable days.

A daily listing lets the visitor choose the date, so four slots that run every Sunday are just four listings — you do not make new ones for each Sunday. There is no separate time field, so the name is what tells a visitor which slot they are booking. Each slot keeps its own Max attendees, counted for each date on its own.
guide.q.one_item_for_many_slots: How do I show one item to visitors instead of every time slot?
guide.a.one_item_for_many_slots:
Put the slots in a group. Tick Hide from public listings list on each slot, and leave the group visible. Your public listings page then shows the group instead of the individual slots. Visitors open the group and pick a slot there.

Set Max Attendees on the group to cap all the slots together. For daily listings that cap is counted for each date, so it works as a limit for the whole day, on top of each slot's own limit.
guide.q.sell_now_for_a_later_season: How do I sell now for dates in a later season?
guide.a.sell_now_for_a_later_season:
A daily listing has no season dates of its own, so you build the season from three settings.

Tick the days it runs under Bookable days. Set Maximum days ahead to reach the last date of the season — it starts at 90 days; enter 0 for no limit. Then add a holiday covering the dates before the season starts, and a second one starting the day after your last date. A holiday blocks its own start and end dates too, so a holiday that starts on your last date takes that date away.

Holidays cover every daily listing on the site, so this sets one season for the whole site — a single listing cannot carry its own season yet. Switching a listing off stops it selling at all, so that is not a way to sell early for a later season.
guide.q.adult_and_child_prices: How do I charge different prices for adults and children?
guide.a.adult_and_child_prices:
A listing holds one ticket price, so each price needs its own listing. There are two ways to arrange them.

A listing for each price. Make an Adults listing and a Children listing, and put them in a group. This is the quicker set-up, but each listing counts its places on its own, so adult places can sell out while child places are still free.

Ticket types as add-ons. Make an Adult ticket listing and a Child ticket listing that carry the real prices. Tick both under Required child listings on each slot, and set the slot's own price to zero. Raise Max tickets per purchase on the slot to the largest group you take, because it starts at 1. The visitor then picks how many tickets they want and splits that number between adults and children, so one set of places covers both.

Set the two ticket listings to Daily as well, and give each the same Bookable days, Minimum days notice, and Maximum days ahead as the slots. A visitor can only pick a date that the slot and the ticket type both allow, so a ticket type left on the 90-day default hides a season further out. Every slot that offers the same ticket type shares its Max attendees for a date, so set that to the total the slots can sell in one day. Keep the ticket listings out of any group with a Max Attendees cap, because one booking would take a place there for the slot and another for the ticket type.
